import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';

report.answer: The low-level streaming engine lives in src/core/streaming.ts (class Stream<Item>, SSE parsing via _iterSSEMessages/SSEDecoder), re-exported from src/streaming.ts. Public resource methods opt into it by returning APIPromise<Stream<T>> when `stream: true` is passed, e.g. chat.completions.create() in src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts (Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>) and responses.create() in src/resources/responses/responses.ts. Higher-level ergonomic wrappers built on top of core Stream live in src/lib/: ChatCompletionStream.ts/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts (used by chat.completions.stream()), AssistantStream.ts (used by beta run-streaming methods), and src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts (used by responses.stream()), all extending the shared EventStream.ts base.

report.answer: The low-level streaming engine lives in src/core/streaming.ts (class Stream<Item>, SSE parsing via _iterSSEMessages/SSEDecoder), re-exported from src/streaming.ts. Public resource methods opt into it by returning APIPromise<Stream<T>> when `stream: true` is passed, e.g. chat.completions.create() in src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts (Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>) and responses.create() in src/resources/responses/responses.ts. Higher-level ergonomic wrappers built on top of core Stream live in src/lib/: ChatCompletionStream.ts/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts (used by chat.completions.stream()), AssistantStream.ts (used by beta run-streaming methods), and src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts (used by responses.stream()), all extending the shared EventStream.ts base.
